project.name: Gridfall
project.description: Isometric tower defense built with Godot 4 + C#. Agent-oriented workflow: a deterministic simulation core, an isometric presentation layer, and a vertical-slice pipeline from requirements analysis through release.
objectives: Keep the simulation deterministic and engine-agnostic so waves, balance, and replays are reproducible
Route design, systems, content, and presentation work to focused agent workspaces with tight load/skip discipline
Move every feature through requirements → design → architecture → build → verify → release as one traceable slice

workspaces.name: game-design
workspaces.description: Requirements analysis, design pillars, feature design, and player-facing intent
responsibilities: Turn raw ideas into requirements with acceptance criteria
Own the design pillars and say no to features that fight them
Define tuning intent (what a knob is for) without setting the numbers

workspaces.name: engine-systems
workspaces.description: Deterministic simulation core, system boundaries, tick model, and architecture decisions
responsibilities: Design the simulation core so it produces identical traces from identical inputs
Hold the Core/View boundary — no Godot types below the boundary
Record every non-obvious technical decision as an ADR

workspaces.name: content-data
workspaces.description: Tower, enemy, wave, and map data plus the balance targets they must hit
responsibilities: Author tower/enemy/wave/map data as plain data, never as code
Prove balance changes against the headless balance sim before they land
Keep every number traceable to a design intent

workspaces.name: presentation
workspaces.description: Isometric rendering, camera, HUD, game feel, and the placeholder → final asset pipeline
responsibilities: Own the projection contract between grid coordinates and screen space
Read simulation state; never mutate it
Keep the board readable at the wave densities the design calls for
Ship placeholders that are functional and cheap, and write the Ludo.ai prompts that replace them

workspaces.name: tooling
workspaces.description: Developer tools — the in-Godot board editor and the headless harness CLIs
responsibilities: Build the board editor as a dev-only scene inside the game project
Keep tools honest — an editor that renders differently from the game is worse than no editor
Own the headless CLIs: the determinism harness and the balance sim runner

workspaces.name: production
workspaces.description: The vertical-slice pipeline — one unit of work moving from requirements to release
responsibilities: Carry exactly one slice at a time through the six stages
Implement against the architecture note, not the requirements
Refuse to release a slice with an unverified acceptance criterion

roles.title: Design Lead
responsibilities: Run requirements analysis on incoming ideas
Write feature design specs and name the tuning knobs

roles.title: Systems Architect
responsibilities: Design simulation systems and their boundaries
Guard determinism and record ADRs

roles.title: Content & Balance Designer
responsibilities: Author and tune tower, enemy, wave, and map data
Run the balance sim and report the deltas

roles.title: Presentation Engineer
responsibilities: Build the isometric view layer, camera, HUD, and input picking
Keep the projection contract in sync with the grid

roles.title: Asset Author
responsibilities: Ship minimal placeholders that make gameplay testable today
Write the Ludo.ai and animation prompts that replace them later

roles.title: Tools Engineer
responsibilities: Build and maintain the in-Godot board editor
Keep the headless CLIs usable by both agents and humans

roles.title: Gameplay Engineer
responsibilities: Implement the slice against the architecture note
Record build decisions as they are made, not afterwards

roles.title: Verification Engineer
responsibilities: Run the determinism harness and the acceptance criteria
On failure, name the single stage the slice loops back to

notes: Gridfall.Core targets net8.0 and must build with zero Godot references
Replays recorded input traces and diffs tick-by-tick state hashes
A slice that touches the core is not verifiable without a green trace diff
Headless N-run wave sim; reports leak rate, gold curve, and time-to-clear
Required before any data change is handed to production
Agents cannot visually verify — compile-check with dotnet build and hand visual sign-off to the human
State plainly in the verify report when something was compile-checked but not seen
Agents write the prompts; the human runs them and tweaks the output in an image editor
Every prompt set names the style anchor and the exact output the pipeline expects
Assets arrive as 2D sprite sheets or 3D .glb — both are supported behind IUnitView (ADR-0004)
Dev-only scene inside the game project; stripped from release builds
Writes map JSON to content-data/maps/ — the same files the game loads
Validates live as you paint, using the game's own validator — errors block save, warnings never do
v1 scope is map geometry, playtest, and live validation. Wave editing is deliberately out
